body:
Source: GitHub issues #651 (bug, P1-high, data loss) and #652 (bug, P1-high, false-green), both in packages/gate-manifest. Re-verified on main @ de8a130a. (a) lib/repair.mjs `repairChain()` (:58-125) is the only write path in the package with no `isSegmentedRepo(dir)` guard — record.mjs:59, enable.mjs, migrate.mjs, migrate-branch.mjs and adopt.mjs all have one. It operates unconditionally on `ledgerPath('manifest', dir)` (:69), renumbers seq from 1, re-serializes every entry and appends a repair record. In a segmented (forest) repo the root is frozen precisely because every segment's first entry carries `anchor: {segment:'root', seq, lineHash}` bound to root's exact raw bytes, so the rewrite makes every anchor mismatch. Repro: root + one segment anchored at root seq 2; `verify` → chain broken at seq 2; `repair-chain --reason … --write` → `repaired …` exit 0; `verify` → `manifest.d/<seg>.jsonl: anchor lineHash mismatch for 'root' seq 2` exit 2. (b) lib/own-chain.mjs:115 `const firstOf = new Map(segments.map((name) => [name, entries.find((entry) => entry.segment === name)]))` resolves each segment's first entry from the LENIENT `readManifestForest` result, which skips malformed lines; a segment whose first line is unparseable yields its SECOND entry, which has no `anchor`, so the walk breaks with `reachedRoot` false and root is dropped with `identityError: null`. Repro: root holds `p5-finding` + `p5-complete`, own segment holds `seg-a` + `seg-b`; truncate the segment's first line → gates `['seg-b']`, identityError null. packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs:207 destructures only `{ entries, identityError }`, so prosecute's open-finding replay sees zero root findings and can complete over an unrefuted finding.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/gate-manifest` is ENFORCEMENT tier: a clean same-model P5 is not sufficient; the parent handles the cross-model attestation ceremony — your job is to report `tier-check`'s exact `git-change:<base>:<digest>` line and which reviewer family reviewed the final commit. Layout: lib/repair.mjs, lib/own-chain.mjs (readOwnManifestChain; `refuse(reason)` sets identityError and empties entries), lib/lineage.mjs (re-exports `firstEntryOf`, `isSegmentedRepo`, `discoverSegments`, `currentBranch`, `recoverOpenSegment`, `MALFORMED_FIRST_ENTRY`, `OVERSIZED_FIRST_ENTRY` from @adlc/tickets/lib/manifest-primitives.mjs — read `firstEntryOf` there: it reads a segment's RAW first line with a byte cap and returns a sentinel on a malformed/oversized line), lib/forest.mjs (readManifestForest — lenient, returns `{entries, skipped}`), lib/record.mjs (RAIL — read its `isSegmentedRepo` guard for the pattern, do not edit), bin/gate-manifest.mjs (read how a thrown Error from `repairChain` is reported — it should surface as the operational error exit 1 with the message). Tests: `npm test -w packages/gate-manifest`; existing own-chain cases in test/own-chain.test.mjs (NOT a rail — extend it or add the new file; say which). Consumers of readOwnManifestChain to re-run read-only: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/*.test.mjs`. Do NOT edit prosecute, runner or adlc-pi.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. `repairChain()` refuses FIRST, before reading or backing anything up, when `isSegmentedRepo(dir)`: it throws an Error whose message starts with `repair-chain refuses to rewrite the frozen root of a segmented repository` and goes on to say every segment anchors to root's exact bytes and to name `migrate-branch`/`adopt` as the forest-mode tools. The refusal applies to dry-run and `--write` alike. ONE exported pure predicate `repairTarget(dir)` → `'root' | 'forest-refused'` is what repairChain consults, so the decision is testable without a ledger.
2. Everything else in repairChain is unchanged for a non-segmented repo (reason length, already-valid refusal, signature checks, backup naming, repair record).
3. `readOwnManifestChain` builds `firstOf` from each VALID segment's RAW first line via `firstEntryOf` (the same reader `lineage.mjs` already uses), not from `entries.find(...)`. When `firstEntryOf` reports a malformed or oversized first line for a segment on the ancestry walk (own or any ancestor it reaches), the function `refuse`s with a reason naming the segment and `first line` — identityError set, entries empty, `skipped` carrying the message — exactly the existing refuse channel, so prosecute (which checks identityError) and the runner (which checks skipped) both fail closed with no change on their side. A valid first line resolves identically to today, so the healthy-chain tests are unchanged.
4. Regression guards: rootless segments (`anchor: null`) still terminate the walk without root; a detached HEAD with segments still refuses with the existing message; `own === null` still returns root's entries; the seq-bound cuts (`upTo`) are untouched.
5. Documentation: `packages/gate-manifest/README.md` — one forest caveat sentence immediately after the `repair-chain` description at :24 and one at the rotation paragraph :461 that mentions `repair-chain`; `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/gate-manifest.mdx` :37 row gains the same caveat, hand-edited. Add one sentence to the own-chain docblock (own-chain.mjs top comment) stating the first entry is read from the raw first line.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 Forest fixture (root + one segment anchored to root, root chain deliberately broken): `repairChain({dir, reason, write: true})` throws the refusal message, root bytes are byte-identical afterwards, no `.pre-repair-*.bak` exists, no repair record was appended; the dry-run form throws the same. verify: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/repair-forest-refusal.test.mjs`
- AC2 Through the bin: `gate-manifest repair-chain --reason "fix the broken root chain" --write --dir <fixture>` exits 1 and stderr contains `refuses to rewrite the frozen root`; a non-segmented broken fixture still repairs exactly as the existing repair tests expect. verify: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/repair-forest-refusal.test.mjs`
- AC3 `repairTarget` → `'forest-refused'` for a dir with the activation marker, `'root'` otherwise; pure (no writes). verify: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/repair-forest-refusal.test.mjs`
- AC4 Own-chain fixture from the issue (root p5-finding + p5-complete; own segment seg-a + seg-b; valid `.lineage`): BEFORE truncation gates are `['p5-finding','p5-complete','seg-a','seg-b']`; AFTER truncating the segment's first line `identityError` is a non-null string naming the segment and `first line`, `entries` is `[]`, and `skipped` contains the same message. verify: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/own-chain-first-line.test.mjs`
- AC5 An ANCESTOR segment (own → mid → root) with a malformed first line refuses the same way; an oversized first line (> MAX_FIRST_LINE_BYTES) refuses; a healthy three-hop chain resolves exactly as before. verify: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/own-chain-first-line.test.mjs`
- AC6 Existing suite green and untouched except where it pinned `entries.find` behaviour (name any rewritten case in the PR body). verify: `npm test -w packages/gate-manifest`
- AC7 Consumers still green with no edits: verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs` and `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs` and `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC8 Docs updated. verify: `grep -c "segmented" packages/gate-manifest/README.md` (>= 2 new mentions near repair-chain; quote lines in the PR body) and `grep -c "segmented" apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/gate-manifest.mdx` (>= 1)
- AC9 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)
- AC10 `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --author-provider anthropic --base origin/main` in the worktree after the final commit reports TRUST-ROOT and prints the `git-change:<base>:<digest>` string; quoted verbatim in the PR body. verify: the command above

OUT OF SCOPE: making prosecute read `skipped` (#652 names it; the refusal above already fails it closed through identityError — file a follow-up), a forest-aware repair tool, lib/record.mjs, lib/verify.mjs, #654/#655/#656.
title: gate-manifest: repair-chain refuses a forest repo, and own-chain resolves a segment's first entry from its raw first line
